analysis:
All three changed files are new test-only files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/: AutopilotBusyReasonTests.swift, AutopilotDownloadFixture.swift and AutopilotDownloadTests.swift. No production source is changed, so no attack surface or control is added here. These tests never reach a shipped binary, and the unit text does not show how the test seams are guarded in production.

What the tests exercise:
- The busy-reason wire vocabulary and the mapping from busy flags to reasons.
- Autopilot download behaviour: the consent-gated effective model set, storage and model-count caps, the closed refusal vocabulary (model_not_selected, autopilot_paused, insufficient_disk, storage_limit_reached, model_limit_reached), failed-self-test refusal by weight hash, the 256-ID bound, and the rule that a downloaded build is neither advertised nor loaded without an Autopilot operation.
- Re-registration only when idle, and registration inventory filtered by the selected set.
- Revoked consent at runtime clearing inventory.
- Restart persistence tied to the recorded weight hash.

This is consistent with A-016, T-052 (shadow evidence is not serving permission) and T-053. The tests assert that no models_update is sent and that nothing is advertised for downloaded builds.

The new surface in the real code, outside these units, is unrequested downloads on the operator's behalf. Production code (autopilotDownloadCoordinator, autopilotRegistrationSeamForTesting, the setters called by the fixtures, and download handling in handlePrefetchModelRequest) was not supplied, so this review cannot confirm that the seams and the download path stay gated by consent and by the private-only setting in production builds. The Autopilot download and set logic deserves review in the non-test source files of the PR.

The fixture overrides process-wide ModelScanner cache state. That is a test-isolation concern only, not a security one. Test inputs are temporary directories and fake weights, with no secrets and no network use (the restart test uses 127.0.0.1:9).

No security regression is identified in the supplied test code.
